text:
lina (Design): Uploaded a quick Figma link for a side-by-side canary diff view + compact timeline scrub. Trying to address: scan speed for engineers, clear affordance for promoting variants, and SR order for snapshots. https://figma.redwood/abc123 :eyes:

sam (Product): first pass: canary column feels dense. Can we reduce duplication between snapshot header and timeline row?

greg (Accessibility): Quick checks: contrast of the promote button label is 3.8:1 — fails AA for normal text. Also screen reader order matters: if snapshots are visually side-by-side, SR should announce them sequentially with headings and percentages.

tara (Frontend): The diff generation on hover could be heavy if we render DOM diffs for every variant. Prefer lazy-render on focus/keyboard navig.

mike (Eng): Agreed. We should compute a compact summary server-side and send a small delta, then render expanded diffs client-side to avoid large payloads.

lina (Design): Proposal: compact summary row always shows: name | baseline % | candidate % | quality delta icon. Click to expand full snapshot diff. Keeps timeline compact.

sam (Product): Suggest microcopy change: current "Promote to Stable" might feel destructive. Maybe "Promote" or "Increase traffic" with confirmation + undo toast.

greg (Accessibility): For toasts, use role="region" and aria-live="polite". For expand/collapse, ensure button has aria-expanded and the panel has aria-labelledby. Add visible focus ring and document 1-2 keyboard shortcuts.

tara (Frontend): Will implement aria-expanded and lazy-render on expand. For keyboard, keep it simple: Tab+Enter to open, Left/Right to move timeline scrubber.

mike (Eng): Left/Right scrubber ok if we throttle events (100ms). Backend: I'll add an endpoint returning diff-summary objects: id, baseline_pct, candidate_pct, score_delta, small_html_snippet.

lina (Design): UX quibble: timeline scrubber overlays version badges and obscures hover affordances. Options: nudge scrubber below badges or make badges sticky/clickable above. Thoughts?

tara (Frontend): Sticky badges via position:sticky is easy on desktop, but for mobile sticky may eat viewport.

sam (Product): Prioritize desktop for next sprint, mobile follow-up. Also add explicit "Compare" mode toggle (side-by-side vs inline diffs) to reduce cognitive load.

greg (Accessibility): In Compare mode, ensure panels have labels like "Baseline (v3.1)" and "Canary (v3.2)". Provide "Skip to next snapshot" links for SR users.

mike (Eng): If we want sharable state, encode compare mode + variant ids in URL (minimal serialization). That helps SRE/QA.

lina (Design): Yes, encode in URL. Keep payload minimal.

sam (Product): Action items: lina update Figma with compact summary row + sticky badges option; tara prototype aria-expanded + lazy-render; mike spec diff-summary endpoint and URL state; greg provide checklist for SR order and contrast targets. Mark high priority for rollout timeline polish.

deploy-bot: Created task RED-UI-4123: "Canary compare: compact summary + a11y fixes" assigned to @lina, @tara, @mike, @greg. Due in 2 weeks.

lina (Design): I'll post updated frames by EOD Friday. Quick note: microcopy alternatives to "Promote traffic": testing "Increase traffic" vs "Move X% to variant".

sam (Product): Prefer concise: "Increase traffic" or just "Promote" with tooltip. Keep buttons short.

greg (Accessibility): SR label should be explicit, e.g., "Promote variant: increase traffic to this version"; tooltip is visual only.

tara (Frontend): Copy acknowledged. I'll wire tooltip and accessible label.

mike (Eng): I'll scope API change and drop PR draft early next week.

lina (Design): Great, thanks everyone. I'll iterate and tag for a final pass. :thumbsup:
